title: Sri Lanka finally get their act together – avoid whitewash | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 14 October 2026 00:06
-     - 14

RAWALPINDI: Sri Lanka finally got their act together to pull off an emphatic eight-wicket win over Pakistan in the third and final T20I played at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium yesterday.

Pakistan by virtue of winning the first two T20Is took the three-match series 2-1. The win, although it was a consolation one, will give a lot of confidence to Sri Lanka and bring momentum to the team going into the One-Day Tri-Series against Pakistan and England.


After their bowlers had managed to keep Pakistan down to a sub-par total of 168-8, Kusal Mendis the Sri Lankan skipper led his team from the front in the run chase with a commanding innings of 87* off 48 balls (9 fours, 4 sixes) to take the Player of the Match award. With his namesake Kamindu Mendis, Kusal figured in an unbroken partnership of 98 off 55 balls to see Sri Lanka home with 17 balls to spare. Kamindu playing the secondary role in the stand made 40* off 27 balls (4 fours).

Sri Lanka lost Lahiru Udara in the second over for 1 falling lbw to Imran Randhawa, a decision which he failed to review for the ball hitting his pads outside the line of off stump. Sineth Jayawardena played a breezy innings of 38 off 26 balls (5 fours, 2 sixes) and helped his captain 59 off 41 balls for the second wicket following the early loss of Udara. From there onwards it was the two Mendis’ who came to the party to wrap it up for Sri Lanka.    

Nuwan Thushara bowled an outstanding final over, conceding just five runs after Pakistan smashed 48 runs in the three overs before that to help themselves to a total of 168-8 after being invited to bat first. Sri Lanka put in a strong performance with both ball and in the field for the first time in the series. But their series nemesis Sahibzada Farhan was once again a thorn in their side scoring 76 off 47 balls (7 fours, 3 sixes), bringing up his third consecutive fifty to take the Player of the Series award.

Farhan however received little support from the top and middle order. Pakistan kept losing wickets before Arafat Minhas walking in at No. 8 smashed an unbeaten 34 off just 20 deliveries (2 fours, 2 sixes) to provide a late boost. The two put on 66 runs off just 37 deliveries. Sri Lanka put on a much better effort with the ball with Vijayakanth Viyaskanth (1/23) playing his first match of the series and Dasun Shanaka (3/23) outstanding in the middle overs.

title: Udara dropped as Sri Lanka struggle for specialist options at the top | Daily FT
summary:
Wednesday, 14 October 2026 00:02
-     - 15

By Sa’adi Thawfeeq

The 15-member Test squad named for Pakistan for the two-match World Test Championship series had quite a few surprises thrown in, most notably the dropping of opening batsman Lahiru Udara after just five Tests, in one of which he scored a splendid 188 against the West Indies in Antigua to draw the Test.

Udara’s surprise exclusion did not go without any notice. Former Sri Lanka Captain Angelo Mathews expressed shock over the decision and warned that such decisions could dent players’ confidence.

“We always talk about building confidence in players but shocked to see Lahiru Udara being left out from the test squad after scoring 188 in the West Indies and failing in just 2 test matches! This will kill his confidence and create doubts in other batters too,” said Mathews in a social media post.

With a grey cloud hanging over the fitness of Pathum Nissanka although he is named in the 15, it would have been pertinent to have picked Udara as one of the specialist openers. The big question is why leave out an opener who has already demonstrated his ability to score a Test century when specialist options at the top appear limited.

If Nissanka is by any chance declared medically unfit, Sri Lanka could be forced to consider alternative opening combinations, including promoting another batter to the top of the order.

The way the team has been selected, Pasindu Sooriyabandara who batted at number 4 and 3 in his proper Test debut against India and scored 80 and 92 could be pushed to open. Sooriyabandara has been a middle order batsman throughout his first-class career where he has accumulated over 5000 runs at an average of 54.46 with 14 centuries which includes four double hundreds. He proved his capabilities as a middle order batter in the Test against India at the SSC.

There was quite a big stir created in the media when Niroshan Dickwella was recalled to the Test side against India. The reason given for his selection over Anjala Bandara was that he was the best wicket-keeper in the business in the country. Dickwella did not disappoint in his return to international cricket scoring a useful 80 and affecting six dismissals behind the stumps although his returns in the next Test were quite ordinary.

With Kusal Mendis returning to the side from injury the wicket-keeper’s berth will be filled but the selectors have also picked Anjala Bandara as reserve wicket-keeper. Mendis is now the all format Captain following the resignation of Dhananjaya de Silva and it will be interesting to see where he bats and whether he will be keeping wickets in his first series as Test Captain.

Uncapped 22-year old Bandara, has been rewarded for a stellar first-class record where he averages 65.85 after 31 games, scoring seven fifties and as many hundreds with a best of 200*.

With Udara, Kamil Mishara with whom he played the second Test against India at the SSC have been dropped along with middle-order batsman Sahan Arachchige who was called up for that Test.

Dinesh Chandimal returns after being subbed out of the first Test at Galle for concussion. The rest of the batting squad remains the same with Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva and Sonal Dinusha.

Sri Lanka has handed out a Test call-up to fast-bowler Eshan Malinga while also recalling left-arm quick Dilshan Madushanka. Malinga has been a regular presence in the shorter formats, this is his first Test call-up, having played 19 first-class matches for 44 wickets at an average of 31.15.

Prabath Jayasuriya and Keshara Nuwantha are the frontline spin options besides all-rounder Sonal Dinusha. The pace attack comprises Milan Rathnayake, Lahiru Kumara and Asitha Fernando besides Malinga and Madushanka, while Vishwa Fernando has been dropped.

The two Tests in Rawalpindi (November 9-13) and Lahore (November 17-21) are both part of the ongoing World Test Championship cycle, where Sri Lanka are currently seventh with a PCT of 33.33 and Pakistan at the bottom with a PCT of 4.63.

Squad: Pathum Nissanka, Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, Sonal Dinusha, Kusal Mendis (Captain), Dhananjaya de Silva, Anjala Bandara, Keshara Nuwantha, Prabath Jayasuriya, Milan Rathnayaka, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka, Eshan Malinga
